Athena's throughput review 20261116-194623-5ksc named the biggest wait in the pipeline and an architectural change that would remove it. Design that change.

Bottleneck: Idle time, not a stage, is the biggest cost: 29,694.5 idle minutes over 518 landings, about 57 minutes per landed job, against a median landed job of 51.7 minutes (THROUGHPUT.md). An inferred, unmeasured share of it is in-job waiting on Git...
Stage: idle
Proposed change: Make CI waits parked, background awaits that release the job's build folder and its drain worker. (1) At the candidate's check stage, a job whose checks go to CI gives up the build folder and its worker after it pushes the candidate. The dr...
Predicted saving: 15.0 minutes per landed job; the median was 51.7 minutes per landed job when the review ran.
Why: THROUGHPUT.md (measured): - Idle between jobs is 29,694.5 min over 518 landings, about 57.3 min per landed job. That is more than the 51.7-min median job (producer 26.4, planning 13.3, checks 1.3, verifier 2.3). - Idle is defined as gaps be...

A change that implements this design must cite throughput review 20261116-194623-5ksc in its request text. The next throughput review then sets the minutes it measured after that change landed against this prediction.

Acceptance:
- A design note under docs/design/ describes the change and how it removes the bottleneck
- The note states the minutes per landed job the change should save and how the next throughput review measures them
